meta.verdict: `inner="exact"` is **usable end-to-end** on all 8 completed ALM trials (p=8/16/64): it returns the same KKT point as multi-start (max ‖Δq‖ 7.9e-10, max |ΔJ| 1.8e-12) with identical feasibility, but it is **37×–64× slower end-to-end** (648.8 ms per 162-path enumeration vs 13.8 ms per 6-start BFGS call; 7–25 enumerations per ALM trial), because the reduced problem is rebuilt and re-solved at every outer iteration. The per-enumeration cost is p-independent (the reduced problem is 10x10 for every p). Completeness is conditional and measured: 89/114 enumerations found the generic 40 finite projective roots (exact=True), 25/114 (21.9%) found only 37-39 and fell back to 64-start BFGS; all reduced matrices were full rank (min eig 8.2e-04) and no KKT Jacobian was singular here, so the fallbacks are homotopy path loss, not rank deficiency (a second complex phase recovered them at ~2.4x cost). The 40-root count is the generic *complex* count (P2-1b), so it is a per-call measured criterion; the unconstrained PSD `Mred` is rank-deficient at noise=0 (rank 8, eig_min ~5e-18) yet still produced 40 finite roots on the 2 probe instances, while ALM's regularised active-set matrices were full rank. **Paper claim:** exact enumeration is a correctness / global-optimality *check* of the inner block at a fixed active set (it agrees with multi-start here, and on every one of 114 probed enumerations a fresh 64-start BFGS found the same global min), not a competitive inner solver; report it as an offline certificate with the fallback rate (21.9%) and the conditional-completeness caveat stated explicitly. Cost lever (measured on 2 trials only, not a general claim): a hybrid schedule that runs exact only at the first outer iteration, or only after the active set has been stable for 2 iterations, reproduces the full-exact J (ΔJ<=9.4e-13) at 4.7-6.8x / 1.1-1.4x lower cost, i.e. still 6-38x slower than pure multi-start -- use it only where a certified inner solve is actually needed.
